title: CapZyme-Seq: A 5′-RNA-Seq Method for Differential Detection and Quantitation of NAD-Capped RNA
author: Vvedenskaya, Nickels
materials: sybr gold nucleic acid gel stain

steps.title: Extract in‑vitro RNA from denaturing gel
steps.instruction: Recover RNA generated in transcription assays by electrophoretic separation, gel excision, elution, and precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Load the sample (from step 6 of the transcription assay) onto a 10 % TBE‑urea slab gel together with a single‑stranded RNA size ladder; run the gel in 1× TBE buffer until the bromophenol‑blue front reaches approximately three‑quarters of the gel length. Use separate gels for each distinct transcription reaction.

Stain the gel with SYBR Gold nucleic‑acid stain, visualize bands under UV illumination, and excise the RNA band of the expected size with a scalpel. Stain gels from different reactions in separate containers.

Prepare a tube‑in‑tube assembly: pierce one to three holes in the bottom of a 0.5 mL low‑binding microfuge tube with a 23‑gauge needle, place this tube inside a 1.7 mL low‑binding microfuge tube, add the gel slices to the upper tube, and centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 2 min (or until all gel fragments pass through the holes into the lower tube).

Add 400 µL gel‑elution buffer (0.3 M NaCl, 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 0.1 mM EDTA) to the crushed gel, incubate the slurry at 70 °C for 10 min, vortex 30 s, transfer the slurry to a Spin‑X filter tube, centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 1 min, and collect the eluate in a 1.7 mL tube.
Remove the remaining crushed gel from the Spin‑X filter, add another 400 µL gel‑elution buffer, and repeat the vortex‑centrifuge‑collect procedure described above.

Combine the two eluates, add 80 µL of 3 M sodium acetate (NaOAc) and 8.8 µL glycogen (10 mg/mL), vortex 30 s, add 650 µL isopropanol, vortex 30 s, and precipitate the RNA by incubating at –80 °C for 16 h (RNA may be stored at –80 °C for ~6 months).

Centrifuge the precipitation at 4 °C for 30 min at 21 000 × g to pellet the RNA, wash the pellet three times with 1 mL 80 % ice‑cold ethanol, air‑dry the pellet for ~5 min, and resuspend in 10 µL nuclease‑free water. Pipette the suspension and incubate on ice for at least 20 min to ensure complete resuspension.

steps.title: Grow E. coli culture and harvest cells
steps.instruction: Prepare mid‑exponential‑phase E. coli cells for RNA isolation.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 mL LB medium to a 15 mL culture tube, inoculate with E. coli, and grow overnight at 37 °C on a roller drum set to 210 rpm.

Transfer 0.5 mL of the overnight culture into 50 mL fresh LB medium contained in a 250 mL DeLong flask; grow at 37 °C on a platform shaker at 210 rpm until the culture reaches mid‑exponential phase (OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.5).

Harvest 2 mL of the cell suspension into 2‑mL tubes, centrifuge for 1 min at 21 000 × g at 25 °C, discard the supernatant, snap‑freeze the cell pellets on dry ice, and store at –80 °C (pellets are stable for ~6 months). Use one pellet for RNA isolation and keep any remaining pellets as backup.

steps.title: Isolate total RNA from harvested E. coli cells
steps.instruction: Extract, DNase‑treat, and purify RNA from frozen cell pellets using TRI Reagent, spin‑column cleanup, and phenol‑chloroform extraction.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the frozen cell pellet in 600 µL TRI Reagent solution, incubate at 70 °C for 10 min, then centrifuge for 10 min at 21 000 × g at 4 °C to pellet insoluble material; transfer the clear supernatant to a fresh tube.

Add 100 % ethanol to the supernatant to reach a final ethanol concentration of 60.5 %, split the mixture evenly between two Direct‑zol spin columns (Zymo Research), and perform on‑column DNase I treatment according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Elute RNA from each column with 30 µL nuclease‑free water pre‑heated to 70 °C; repeat the elution two additional times, then pool all eluates.
Add 10 µL TURBO DNase 10× buffer and 1 µL TURBO DNase to the pooled RNA and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min to remove residual DNA.
Purify the DNase‑treated RNA by acid phenol:chloroform (pH 4.5):
a. Adjust the RNA volume to 200 µL with nuclease‑free water, add 200 µL acid phenol/chloroform (pH 4.5), and vortex 10 s.
b. Centrifuge 30 s at 21 000 × g at 25 °C and collect the upper aqueous phase.

c. Add 200 µL chloroform, vortex 10 s, centrifuge 30 s at 21 000 × g at 25 °C, discard the bulk of the lower organic phase, then centrifuge 1 min at 21 000 × g at 25 °C and discard any residual organic phase.

d. Add 20 µL 3 M NaOAc and 2.2 µL glycogen (10 mg/mL), vortex 30 s, add 670 µL 100 % ethanol, vortex 30 s, and precipitate the RNA by incubating at –80 °C for 16 h (RNA may be stored at –80 °C for ~6 months).
e. Centrifuge at 4 °C for 30 min at 21 000 × g to pellet the RNA, wash the pellet three times with 1 mL 80 % ice‑cold ethanol.

f. Air‑dry the pellet for ~5 min, resuspend in 50 µL nuclease‑free water, pipette, and incubate on ice for at least 20 min to achieve complete dissolution; determine RNA concentration with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer (typical yield ≈ 60 µg from 2 mL culture).
